Author: Rick Ashford <rick@theashfords.org>
Date:   Fri Jul 31 15:43:33 2026 -0500

    docs: record block-package endpoint inference and ground-truth reconciliation
    
    The block endpoint is undocumented. This records the inference made before any
    capture, then scores it against the real requests, so the reasoning can be
    judged rather than just the result.
    
    Verified against the live API:
    
      BLOCK    POST /api/packages/{locator}/rules   {"policyIds":[..],"versions":"ALL"|[..]}
      UNBLOCK  PUT  /api/policies/{policyId}/rules  [ ..surviving rule objects.. ]
    
    Findings that outlive this feature:
    
    * Bearer API-token auth reaches these endpoints. A cookie session gets 403 —
      FOSSA's CSRF protection is session-only — so the server can call them but a
      browser-derived flow cannot without the _csrf token.
    * GET /api/policies lists every policy with its rules. DECISIONS.md §5 says no
      list-policies endpoint exists; that is true of the vendored spec and false of
      the live API.
    * Block rules are QUALITY-policy rules of type blacklisted_dependency. The
      §5 claim that FOSSA has no per-package block primitive is wrong, and the
      security-policy tools are not the blocking mechanism.
    * Unblock is read-modify-write over the whole rule set with no precondition
      mechanism, so concurrent unblocks silently clobber each other.
    
    No tools yet; this is the brief they get written from.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

3	
4	## Where things stand
5	
6	Two parallel workstreams, both at clean boundaries.
7

9	discovery is *complete and verified against the live API*. The brief is committed as

16	`api-parity`, 281 tests passing, unpushed. **None of these tools are registered in `server.py`

18	
19	## Decisions made (and why)
20	
21	- **`models.py` became a package** (`models/__init__.py` + one module per domain, mirroring
22	  `tools/`). This was the enabling move for running four domain agents in parallel — otherwise
23	  every agent edits one file simultaneously and loses work. Import surface unchanged; domain models
24	  are imported from their own module (`from ..models.projects import …`), not re-exported.
25	- **No new env vars.** The user explicitly chose the existing `FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES` (not a new
26	  `FOSSA_MCP_ENABLE_WRITE=1`) and `FOSSA_API_TOKEN` (not `FOSSA_API_KEY`). The tiered gate in
27	  `writes.py` already implements "read-only by default"; a second parallel gate would just be a
28	  second thing to misconfigure.
29	- **Tool registration in `server.py` and the tier sets in `tests/test_mcp_integration.py` are held
30	  centrally**, not done by the domain agents, because parallel edits to those two files collide.
31	  Each agent's registration snippet is in its commit message / was reported; re-derive from the
32	  tool functions if needed.
33	- **`docs/ENDPOINT_INFERENCE.md` records the inference made *before* ground truth, then scores it.**
34	  The reasoning is itself a deliverable Chelsea asked for — do not tidy the misses out of it.
35

38	- `docs/ENDPOINT_INFERENCE.md` — the block-endpoint brief. Committed on `block-package-tools`.
39	- `src/fossa_mcp/models/` — new package; `__init__.py` is the old `models.py` plus a docstring

48	**Verified — live API calls, this session:**
49	
50	```
51	BLOCK    POST /api/packages/{locator}/rules   {"policyIds":[266648],"versions":"ALL"|["3.11.1"]}
52	UNBLOCK  PUT  /api/policies/{policyId}/rules  [ …bare array of surviving rule objects… ]
53	READ     GET  /api/policies        (all policies + full rule sets)
54	READ     GET  /api/policies/{id}
55	```
56	
57	- The unblock body is a **bare top-level array**, not `{"rules":[…]}`. The wrapper forms return an
58	  opaque 500. Each element is a full rule object exactly as `GET /api/policies/{id}` returns it,

60	- **Bearer `FOSSA_API_TOKEN` auth reaches these endpoints.** A cookie-authenticated browser request
61	  gets `403 "Missing or invalid authentication"` — FOSSA's CSRF (`<meta name="_csrf">`) is
62	  session-only. This is what makes the tools possible.
63	- Block is **idempotent**: re-posting returns the same `policyVersionId` and reuses the same
64	  `ruleId`. Earns `idempotentHint=True`.
65	- Block rules are `type: "blacklisted_dependency"` on a **QUALITY** policy. The UI's policy selector
66	  offers only quality policies. Chelsea's correction is confirmed empirically, not just on authority.
67	- Unblock is **read-modify-write with no precondition mechanism** (no ETag / `If-Match`;

69	- `DELETE /api/packages/{locator}/rules` → 404. No symmetric delete.

1	# Inferring the block-package endpoint
2	
3	**Status: inference only. No request has been sent to any endpoint named here.**
4	
5	Written before ground truth was captured, so that the inference can be scored honestly against
6	the real request. Section 5 is left empty on purpose and is filled in after the capture.
7	
8	Source of evidence: `spec/fossa-openapi.json`, FOSSA API 4.34.55, vendored in this repo. 271
9	documented operations. Every claim below about "the documented surface" is checkable against that
10	file.
11	
12	---
13	
14	## 1. What the documented API does and does not contain
15	
16	**There is no policy-rule surface in the documented API at all.** Searching all 191 documented
17	paths for policy, rule, block, quality:
18	
19	| Path | Methods | What it actually does |
20	|------|---------|----------------------|
21	| `/organizations/{id}/settings/projects/issues/quality` | GET, PUT, PATCH | Org-level defaults: `defaultQualityPolicyId`, scanning and status-check toggles |
22	| `/v2/projects/policy` | PUT | Assigns an existing policy id to projects |
23	| `/v2/release-groups/policy` | PUT | Same, for release groups |
24	
25	Zero occurrences of `blockRule`, `block_rule`, `blocklist`, or `denylist` anywhere in the spec.
26	There is no `/policies` collection, no create-policy, no list-policies, and no rules sub-resource.
27	
28	`qualityPolicyId` appears 19 times, but only ever as an **integer field being assigned** to
29	something that already exists:
30	
31	```
32	PUT /projects/{locator}      qualityPolicyId: integer, nullable
33	POST /project_group          qualityPolicyId: integer, nullable
34	PUT  /project_group/{groupId} qualityPolicyId: integer, nullable
35	```
36	
37	The `PUT /projects/{locator}` field carries a description that is the most useful single sentence
38	in the spec for this problem:
39	
40	> "ID of the quality policy to apply to this project. Requires SetPolicy permission for QUALITY
41	> policy type."
42	
43	Two things follow. Policies are **typed** — the four types are LICENSING (`policyId`), SECURITY
44	(`securityPolicyId`), QUALITY (`qualityPolicyId`), SBOM (`sbomPolicyId`) — and policy authorship
45	lives behind a distinct `SetPolicy` permission on a policy *type*. A block rule is a change to a
46	QUALITY policy's contents, which is a different operation from assigning that policy to a project,
47	and only the latter is documented.
48	
49	So the block endpoint is genuinely undocumented rather than merely hard to find. The inference below
50	is built from FOSSA's conventions in adjacent, documented, package-level operations.
51	
52	## 2. The closest documented analogue
53	
54	`license-conclusions` is the strongest signal in the spec. It is a package-level decision that
55	changes how policy evaluates that package, exposed as a **pair of verb-suffixed sibling paths**:
56	
57	```
58	PUT /license-conclusions/conclude     Add a license to the license conclusions for a dependency revision
59	PUT /license-conclusions/unconclude   Remove a license from the license conclusions for a dependency revision
60	```
61	
62	That is the same problem shape as block/unblock: an operator-applied, reversible, package-scoped
63	verdict that policy then respects. Note what FOSSA did *not* do here — it did not model the
64	conclusion as a resource with `POST` to create and `DELETE` to remove. It used `PUT` on a named
65	action, with the target carried in the body. I weight this heavily.
66	
67	The second analogue is `package-label-assignments`, which is how FOSSA addresses *a package* rather
68	than a dependency revision:
69	
70	```json
71	POST /package-label-assignments
72	{
73	  "packageId":      "string  (required)",
74	  "packageVersion": "string  (optional — blank for all versions)",
75	  "scope":          "org | project | revision  (required)",
76	  "scopeId":        "string",
77	  "labelIds":       [1, 2]
78	}
79	```
80	
81	Two distinct package-identity conventions therefore exist in the documented surface:
82	
83	* `dependencyRevisionLocator` — one full locator string, e.g. `pip+mcp$1.6.0` (license-conclusions)
84	* `packageId` + optional `packageVersion` — split, with **blank version meaning all versions**
85	  (package-label-assignments)
86	
87	For blocking, the split form is the better fit and I predict it: a block rule that cannot say "all
88	versions of `mcp`" would be close to useless, and the split form is exactly how FOSSA already
89	expresses that.
90	
91	Scoping is always explicit and enumerated, never implied. License-conclusions uses a `oneOf`
92	discriminated on a `scope` string (`project` requires `projectLocator`; `revision` requires both
93	locators); label assignments use a flat `scope` enum plus `scopeId`. Neither ever defaults to
94	org-wide silently.
95	
96	## 3. Path-shape conventions
97	
98	Sorting the documented paths by style rather than by tag:
99	
100	* **Unversioned plural-noun collections** are the recent style: `/license-conclusions`,
101	  `/package-labels`, `/package-label-assignments`, `/custom-risk-scores`, `/issue-filters`,
102	  `/issue_counts`.
103	* **`/v2/` paths** are the paginated bulk reads and the bulk mutations: `/v2/projects`,
104	  `/v2/issues`, `/v2/revisions/{locator}/dependencies`.
105	* **Bulk variants take a `/bulk` suffix**: `POST /package-label-assignments/bulk`.
106	* Identity for these newer collections is carried **in the body, not the path** — note that
107	  `POST`, `PUT`, and `DELETE /package-label-assignments` all address the collection path, with the
108	  target in the body.
109	* Query strings are parsed with `qs`: arrays as `labels[]=`, nested as
110	  `excludeFields[packageLabels][0]=`.
111	* Locators in path position are URL-encoded whole (`git%2Bgithub.com%2Facme%2Fwidget`), since they
112	  contain `+`, `/`, and `$`.
113	
114	A block feature is newer than the v2 bulk endpoints, so I expect **unversioned**, not `/v2/`.
115	
116	## 4. Predictions
117	
118	Ranked. All are under the `https://app.fossa.com/api` base.
119	
120	### C1 — paired verb actions on a rules collection · confidence: moderate (~40%)
121	
122	```
123	PUT /api/quality-policy-rules/block
124	PUT /api/quality-policy-rules/unblock
125	```
126	
127	```json
128	{
129	  "qualityPolicyId": 123,
130	  "packageId":       "pip+mcp",
131	  "packageVersion":  "",
132	  "scope":           "org",
133	  "scopeId":         "…"
134	}
135	```
136	
137	Direct application of the `license-conclusions/conclude|unconclude` pattern to the resource
138	Chelsea named. Plausible alternative spellings of the collection segment, in order:
139	`/policy-rules`, `/package-rules`, `/blocked-packages`, `/quality-rules`.
140	
141	### C2 — REST-nested rules under the policy · confidence: low-moderate (~25%)
142	
143	```
144	POST   /api/policies/{policyId}/rules      {"type": "BLOCK", "packageId": "pip+mcp", …}
145	DELETE /api/policies/{policyId}/rules/{ruleId}
146	```
147	
148	The canonical REST modeling, and the shape most other vendors would ship. I rank it below C1
149	because FOSSA demonstrably chose verb-suffixed pairs over resource-CRUD for the one documented
150	operation of this kind, and because unblock-by-`ruleId` would force a list-rules call first — an
151	endpoint that does not exist in the documented surface either.
152	
153	### C3 — action on the package · confidence: low (~15%)
154	
155	```
156	POST /api/v2/dependencies/{locator}/block
157	```
158	
159	Reads naturally against the documented `GET /v2/dependencies/{locator}`, but it buries the policy
160	that receives the rule. With four policy types and multiple policies per type, the target policy
161	has to be addressable, and this shape has nowhere to put it except a query parameter.
162	
163	### C4 — whole-policy replace · confidence: low (~15%)
164	
165	```
166	PUT /api/policies/{policyId}      { …entire policy including full rules array… }
167	```
168	
169	FOSSA's v1 style does do this — `PUT /projects/{locator}` accepts 53 fields and replaces the
170	project. If block is implemented as "GET the policy, append a rule, PUT it back," then a
171	single-package block tool has a read-modify-write race and cannot be made safe without optimistic
172	concurrency. **This is the outcome I most want ruled out**, because it changes the tool's design
173	rather than just its URL.
174	
175	### Shape predictions, held with higher confidence than any path
176	
177	These are what I would actually bet on, and they are what the reconciliation should score:
178	
179	1. Package identity is `packageId` + optional `packageVersion`, with empty version meaning all
180	   versions — **not** a single `dependencyRevisionLocator`. (~65%)
181	2. The scope is explicit and enumerated from `org` / `project` / `revision`, never implicit. (~80%)
182	3. The quality policy is addressed by **numeric id**, consistent with every other policy reference
183	   in the API. (~85%)
184	4. Block and unblock are **two paths**, not one path with a boolean or a `DELETE`. (~60%)
185	5. The path is **unversioned**, not under `/v2/`. (~70%)
186	6. The response echoes the created rule, including a server-assigned numeric rule id. (~55%)
187	
188	## 5. Inferred vs. actual
189	
190	Captured 2026-07-31 from live UI traffic against the Ash4d org, package `pip+aiofile`.
191	
192	### The endpoints
193	
194	```
195	BLOCK    POST /api/packages/pip%2Baiofile/rules          -> 200
196	UNBLOCK  PUT  /api/policies/266648/rules                 -> 200
197	READ     GET  /api/policies                              -> 200   (all policies, with rules)
198	READ     GET  /api/policies/266648                       -> 200
199	```
200	
201	Block and unblock are **not a symmetric pair**. Block is package-scoped and additive. Unblock is
202	policy-scoped and replaces the policy's whole rule set — it is the policy editor's Save, not a
203	delete of a named rule.
204	
205	### Auth: the API token works, CSRF applies only to the browser
206	
207	A cookie-authenticated `POST` from the page returns `403 "Missing or invalid authentication"` —
208	FOSSA's app carries `<meta name="_csrf">` / `window._csrf` and writes require it. That protection is
209	session-only. With `Authorization: Bearer $FOSSA_API_TOKEN` and no CSRF header, both reads and
210	writes succeed. **These endpoints are reachable from a token-authenticated server**, which is what
211	makes the tools possible at all.
212	
213	### Block request schema — verified
214	
215	```
216	POST /api/packages/{packageLocator}/rules
217	{ "policyIds": [266648], "versions": "ALL" }
218	```
219	
220	* `policyIds` — array of numeric policy ids. Only `QUALITY` policies are offered by the UI.
221	* `versions` — `"ALL"`, or an array of version strings. `[]` is accepted and behaves as all.
222	  A JSON object 400s with `Invalid versions: …`. Omitting it 400s with
223	  `Missing versions in request body`.
224	* Response is the policy version array, e.g.
225	  `[{"id":359431,"policyId":266648,"rulesHash":"53e41a0d…","defaultAction":"APPROVE",…}]`.
226	* **Idempotent.** Re-posting an identical block returns the same `policyVersionId` and reuses the
227	  same `ruleId` rather than creating a duplicate, consistent with the `rulesHash` keying.
228	
229	### Unblock request schema — verified
230	
231	```
232	PUT /api/policies/{policyId}/rules
233	[ {…rule…}, {…rule…} ]
234	```
235	
236	The body is a **bare top-level JSON array** of the rules that should survive — not an object.
237	`{"rules":[…]}`, `{"rules":[…ruleIds…]}` and `{"ruleIds":[…]}` all return an opaque `500`; the
238	wrapper is the whole reason. `DELETE /api/packages/{locator}/rules` is a `404`, so there is no
239	symmetric delete on the package resource.
240	
241	Each element is a full rule object exactly as `GET /api/policies/{policyId}` returns it, including
242	`ruleId`, `createdAt`/`updatedAt`, every `dependency*` field (nulls included), and the
243	`PolicyVersionRule` join object. Removing a block means fetching the policy, filtering out the
244	`blacklisted_dependency` rule whose `packageProjectLocator` matches, and PUTting the remainder.
245	
246	**This is read-modify-write on the entire rule set, and it is the design constraint of this
247	feature.** Two callers unblocking different packages concurrently will silently clobber each
248	other — the last PUT wins and reinstates whatever the other removed. The tool must fetch
249	immediately before writing and should surface the rule set it is about to send. There is no ETag,
250	`If-Match`, or version parameter to make it safe; `rulesHash` is returned but not accepted as a
251	precondition.
252	
253	### The rule that a block creates
254	
255	```json
256	{
257	  "ruleId": 58586851,
258	  "type": "blacklisted_dependency",
259	  "packageProjectLocator": "pip+aiofile",
260	  "dependencyFilterVersionType": "ALL",
261	  "dependencyFilterName": null,
262	  "dependencyFilterStartVersion": null,
263	  "dependencyFilterEndVersion": null,
264	  "enabled": true,
265	  "notes": null,
266	  "PolicyVersionRule": { "policyVersionId": 359431, "ruleId": 58586851 }
267	}
268	```
269	
270	Attached to policy **266648 "Major - 3 Policy", type `QUALITY`**. The block dialog's POLICIES
271	multi-select offered exactly one option — that quality policy. No licensing, security, or SBOM
272	policy was selectable.
273	
274	### Scoring
275	
276	| # | Prediction | Actual | Verdict |
277	|---|---|---|---|
278	| C1 | `PUT /api/quality-policy-rules/block` + `/unblock` | `POST /api/packages/{locator}/rules`; `PUT /api/policies/{id}/rules` | **Miss** on path |
279	| — | Block is a *rule* attached to a *policy* | Dialog: "Create a new rule blocking this package"; rule row on the policy | **Hit** |
280	| 1 | Identity is `packageId` + optional version, blank = all versions | Versionless locator `pip+aiofile`, but in the **path**; version scope via `dependencyFilterVersionType: "ALL"` | **Partial** — right identity, wrong placement, richer version model |
281	| 2 | Explicit `org`/`project`/`revision` scope enum | No such scope. Scope *is* which policies the rule attaches to | **Miss** |
282	| 3 | Policy addressed by numeric id | `266648` | **Hit** |
283	| 4 | Block and unblock are two paths | Two paths — but different resources, not sibling verbs | **Hit on form, miss on shape** |
284	| 5 | Unversioned path, not `/v2/` | `/api/packages/…`, `/api/policies/…`; `GET /api/v2/policies` returns 404 | **Hit** |
285	| 6 | Response echoes a server-assigned numeric rule id | Rule carries `ruleId`; POST response body not inspected | **Unverified** |
286	| C4 | Whole-policy read-modify-write — "the outcome I most want ruled out" | **Realized for unblock.** `PUT /api/policies/{id}/rules` sends the surviving rule set | **Confirmed concern** |
287	
288	Where the reasoning worked: the license-conclusions analogy correctly predicted an unversioned,
289	body-carrying, non-CRUD design, and correctly predicted that the package is addressed by a
290	versionless locator. Where it failed: I assumed FOSSA would model block/unblock as one resource
291	with two verbs, because that is what `conclude`/`unconclude` does. It instead split them across two
292	resources with different owners — the package for creation, the policy for removal — which no
293	amount of staring at the documented surface would have revealed.
294	
295	### Two findings that change the repo beyond this feature
296	
297	1. **`GET /api/policies` exists and lists every policy with its full rule set**, including
298	   `policyId`, `type` (`LICENSING`/`SECURITY`/`QUALITY`/`SBOM`), `title`, and `latestVersion`.
299	   `DECISIONS.md` §5 states there is "no create-policy or list-policies endpoint in the vendored
300	   spec, so policies are authored in the FOSSA web app and addressed here by the numeric id in
301	   their URL." That is true of the *documented* spec and false of the *live* API. Callers no longer
302	   need to read ids out of URLs.
303	2. **Policies are versioned and rules attach to a `policyVersionId`.** Adding the block rule moved
304	   the quality policy from version `359271` to `359431`; removing it returned it to `359271` rather
305	   than minting a third version, which is consistent with FOSSA keying versions on the
306	   `rulesHash` present in each `latestVersion`. Any write tool must therefore treat a policy edit
307	   as producing a new version, and the `PUT /rules` replace is a lost-update risk if two callers
308	   edit one policy concurrently.
309	
310	## 6. Standing caveat for the implementation
311	
312	Whatever the capture shows, the resulting tools are built on an endpoint FOSSA does not document
313	and does not owe anyone stability on. It can change without notice or a version bump, and the
314	contract tests in this repo pin our *request* shape — they cannot detect FOSSA changing its side.
315	The README must say so at the point of use, and the tools should fail loudly rather than degrade
316	quietly if the response shape stops matching.
317	
318	---
319	
320	## Appendix: correction to a prior finding in this repo
321	
322	`DECISIONS.md` §5 currently states that FOSSA has no per-package block primitive, and that a
323	package is blocked by an assigned *security* policy raising a vulnerability issue plus the CI
324	status check failing the build — concluding that `fossa_enable_security_policy` "is the block."
325	
326	That was inferred from the documented surface, where no policy-rule endpoint of any kind appears,
327	and it is wrong. Block rules belong to the **quality** policy, per Chelsea Boling (Principal CS
328	Engineer, FOSSA) correcting it directly.
329	
330	The correction is now confirmed empirically, not just on authority. A block creates a
331	`blacklisted_dependency` rule on a `QUALITY` policy (section 5), and the block dialog's policy
332	selector offers **only** quality policies — a security policy cannot receive a block rule at all.
333	FOSSA does have a per-package block primitive; it is simply not reachable from the documented API.
334	
335	`DECISIONS.md` §5 needs amending on both counts: the "no per-package block primitive" claim and the
336	"no list-policies endpoint" claim are both false of the live API. The security-policy tools stay as
337	they are — they do real work, assigning a security policy and enabling its enforcement — they are
338	simply not the blocking mechanism.
339

1	"""Write-tier gating shared by every tool that modifies FOSSA state.
2	
3	The FOSSA write surface is 114 operations and they are not one risk. Assigning a
4	security policy, deleting every project matching a filter, and replacing an
5	organization's SAML configuration all "write", but an operator who wants the
6	first does not thereby want the third. So the gate is tiered, and each tier is
7	enabled independently:
8	
9	* `WriteTier.WRITE` — create and update. `FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES`.
10	* `WriteTier.DESTRUCTIVE` — deletes, and operations whose target set is
11	  unbounded (bulk endpoints that accept a filter rather than a list of ids).
12	  `FOSSA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE`, **and** `FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES`.
13	* `WriteTier.ADMIN` — identity, authentication, and access control: SAML, OIDC,
14	  roles, service accounts, team membership. `FOSSA_ALLOW_ADMIN`, **and**
15	  `FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES`.
16	
17	The higher tiers deliberately do not imply the lower one in either direction.
18	`FOSSA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true` alone grants nothing; it is a qualifier on writes,
19	not a replacement for enabling them. This means the safe default survives a
20	half-configured deployment: a missing `FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES` disables everything
21	regardless of what else is set.
22	
23	Why this exists at all: under DECISIONS.md §2 the server authenticates no
24	callers and executes every request with one shared token. Anyone who reaches the
25	HTTP transport inherits whatever tiers are on. The gate is the only thing
26	between a misread tool call and an irreversible change, so it is checked in the
27	tool body before any request is constructed — never at registration time, and
28	never by the caller.
29	"""
30	
31	from enum import Enum
32	
33	from .config import Settings
34	from .errors import FossaWriteNotPermittedError
35	
36	
37	class WriteTier(Enum):
38	    """How much trust a write tool requires before it may run."""
39	
40	    WRITE = "write"
41	    DESTRUCTIVE = "destructive"
42	    ADMIN = "admin"
43	
44	
45	_TIER_SETTING = {
46	    WriteTier.DESTRUCTIVE: ("fossa_allow_destructive", "FOSSA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE"),
47	    WriteTier.ADMIN: ("fossa_allow_admin", "FOSSA_ALLOW_ADMIN"),
48	}
49	
50	_TIER_RATIONALE = {
51	    WriteTier.DESTRUCTIVE: "deletes FOSSA state or acts on an unbounded set of targets",
52	    WriteTier.ADMIN: "changes identity, authentication, or access control",
53	}
54	
55	
56	def require_tier(settings: Settings, tier: WriteTier, tool_name: str) -> None:
57	    """Refuse a write before any request is constructed.
58	
59	    Raises:
60	        FossaWriteNotPermittedError: If the tool's tier is not enabled. The
61	            message names the tool, the reason it is gated, and the exact
62	            environment variable to set, so the refusal is actionable rather
63	            than a bare denial.
64	    """
65	    if not settings.fossa_allow_writes:
66	        raise FossaWriteNotPermittedError(
67	            f"{tool_name} modifies FOSSA state and FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES is not enabled. "
68	            f"Set FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES=true to permit it."
69	        )
70	
71	    if tier is WriteTier.WRITE:
72	        return
73	
74	    attribute, env_var = _TIER_SETTING[tier]
75	    if not getattr(settings, attribute):
76	        raise FossaWriteNotPermittedError(
77	            f"{tool_name} {_TIER_RATIONALE[tier]}, which requires the {tier.value} tier. "
78	            f"FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES is enabled but {env_var} is not. "
79	            f"Set {env_var}=true to permit it."
80	        )
81	
82	
83	__all__ = ["WriteTier", "require_tier"]
84

7	What FOSSA's API actually supports, which is what shapes these tools:
8

10	  and no list-policies endpoint in the vendored OpenAPI spec, so a policy is
11	  addressed here by the numeric id shown in its FOSSA URL.
12	* There is no per-package "block" primitive. FOSSA blocks a package by raising
13	  a vulnerability issue against it under an assigned security policy, and then
14	  failing the CI status check. `enable_security_policy` turns exactly that
15	  combination on; it is the block.
16	"""

41	async def _fetch_baseline(
42	    client: FossaClient, settings: Settings, project_locator: str
43	) -> FossaSecurityBaseline:
44	    """Read FOSSA's currently-configured security enforcement for one project.
45	
46	    The org-level default is only fetched when `FOSSA_ORG_ID` is configured;
47	    without it the project's own assignment still resolves, and
48	    `org_default_security_policy_id` is reported as unknown rather than guessed.
49	    """
50	    encoded_locator = quote(project_locator, safe="")
51	    project = await client.request_json("GET", f"/projects/{encoded_locator}")
52	    project_data = project if isinstance(project, dict) else {}
53	
54	    org_default_policy_id: int | None = None
55	    status_check_filter: int | None = None
56	
57	    if settings.fossa_org_id is not None:
58	        org_settings = await client.request_json(
59	            "GET", f"/organizations/{settings.fossa_org_id}/settings/projects/issues/security"
60	        )
61	        if isinstance(org_settings, dict):

63	            status_check_filter = _as_int(
64	                org_settings.get("projectDefaultStatusCheckFilterVulnerability")
65	            )
66	
67	    return FossaSecurityBaseline(
68	        project_locator=project_locator,
69	        security_policy_id=_as_int(project_data.get("securityPolicyId")),
70	        org_default_security_policy_id=org_default_policy_id,
71	        security_issue_scanning_enabled=_as_bool(project_data.get("securityIssueScanningEnabled")),
72	        security_status_check_enabled=_as_bool(project_data.get("securityStatusCheckEnabled")),
73	        status_check_filter_vulnerability=status_check_filter,
74	    )

78	    """Coerce a FOSSA JSON value to `int`, or `None` if it is absent or not one."""
79	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
80	        return None
81	    return value

84	def _as_bool(value: Any) -> bool | None:
85	    """Coerce a FOSSA JSON value to `bool`, or `None` if it is absent or not one."""
86	    return value if isinstance(value, bool) else None

89	async def get_security_policy(
90	    ctx: Context,
91	    project_locator: str,
92	) -> dict[str, Any]:
93	    """

95	    enforce, plus the local overlay layered on top of it.
96	
97	    Read-only. The overlay can only make enforcement stricter, never looser.
98	    """
99	    validated = SecurityPolicyReadInput(project_locator=project_locator)
100	
101	    lifespan_ctx = ctx.request_context.lifespan_context
102	    client: FossaClient = lifespan_ctx["client"]
103	    settings: Settings = lifespan_ctx["settings"]
104	
105	    baseline = await _fetch_baseline(client, settings, validated.project_locator)
106	    document = load_policy_document(settings.fossa_policy_file)
107	
108	    overlay: dict[str, Any] = {
109	        "policy_file": settings.fossa_policy_file,
110	        "loaded": document is not None,
111	        "policies": [
112	            policy.model_dump(mode="json") for policy in (document.security if document else [])
113	        ],
114	    }
115	
116	    return {
117	        "ok": True,
118	        "endpoint": (
119	            "GET /projects/{locator} + GET /organizations/{id}/settings/projects/issues/security"
120	        ),
121	        "data": {
122	            "baseline": baseline.model_dump(mode="json"),
123	            "effective_fossa_policy_id": baseline.effective_policy_id,
124	            "overlay": overlay,
125	        },

129	async def evaluate_security_policy(
130	    ctx: Context,
131	    project_locator: str,
132	    revision_locator: str,
133	    depths: list[DependencyDepth] | None = None,
134	    count: int = 100,
135	) -> PolicyEvaluation:
136	    """
137	    Evaluate every dependency in a revision against the effective security
138	    policy and return an allow/warn/block verdict per package.
139	
140	    Read-only: this reports what the policy says, it does not apply anything to
141	    FOSSA. A FOSSA-raised vulnerability always blocks and cannot be cleared by a
142	    local exception.
143	    """
144	    validated = PolicyEvaluateInput(
145	        project_locator=project_locator,
146	        revision_locator=revision_locator,
147	        depths=depths,
148	        count=count,
149	    )
150	
151	    lifespan_ctx = ctx.request_context.lifespan_context
152	    client: FossaClient = lifespan_ctx["client"]
153	    settings: Settings = lifespan_ctx["settings"]
154	
155	    if not (1 <= validated.count <= settings.fossa_max_page_size):
156	        raise ValueError(f"Count must be between 1 and {settings.fossa_max_page_size}")
157

168	
169	    params: list[tuple[str, str]] = [("page", "1"), ("count", str(validated.count))]
170	    for depth in validated.depths or []:
171	        params.append(("depth[]", depth))
172	
173	    body = await client.request_json(
174	        "GET", f"/v2/revisions/{encoded_locator}/dependencies", params=params
175	    )

177	
178	    return evaluate_dependencies(
179	        revision_locator=full_revision_locator,
180	        dependencies=[dep for dep in dependencies if isinstance(dep, dict)],
181	        baseline=baseline,

193	    """Return the full `project$revision` locator the dependencies path wants."""
194	    prefix = f"{project_locator}$"
195	    if revision_locator.startswith(prefix):

197	    return f"{project_locator}${revision_locator}"

200	async def enable_security_policy(
201	    ctx: Context,
202	    project_locator: str,
203	    security_policy_id: int,
204	    enable_scanning: bool = True,
205	    enable_status_check: bool = True,
206	) -> dict[str, Any]:
207	    """
208	    Assign a FOSSA security policy to a project and turn on the enforcement that
209	    blocks packages violating it.
210	
211	    WRITES TO FOSSA. Requires FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES=true.
212	
213	    Blocking in FOSSA is the combination of an assigned security policy (which
214	    decides what counts as a violation), security issue scanning (which finds
215	    violations), and the security status check (which fails the build). This
216	    tool sets all three. `security_policy_id` is the numeric id from the
217	    policy's FOSSA URL; the API exposes no way to list policies.
218	    """
219	    validated = PolicyEnableInput(
220	        project_locator=project_locator,
221	        security_policy_id=security_policy_id,
222	        enable_scanning=enable_scanning,
223	        enable_status_check=enable_status_check,
224	    )
225	
226	    lifespan_ctx = ctx.request_context.lifespan_context
227	    client: FossaClient = lifespan_ctx["client"]
228	    settings: Settings = lifespan_ctx["settings"]
229	
230	    require_tier(settings, WriteTier.WRITE, "fossa_enable_security_policy")
231	
232	    before = await _fetch_baseline(client, settings, validated.project_locator)
233	
234	    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
235	        "securityPolicyId": validated.security_policy_id,
236	        "securityIssueScanningEnabled": validated.enable_scanning,
237	        "securityStatusCheckEnabled": validated.enable_status_check,
238	    }
239	
240	    encoded_locator = quote(validated.project_locator, safe="")
241	    result = await client.request_json("PUT", f"/projects/{encoded_locator}", json_body=payload)
242	
243	    after = await _fetch_baseline(client, settings, validated.project_locator)
244	
245	    return {
246	        "ok": True,
247	        "endpoint": "PUT /projects/{locator}",
248	        "data": {
249	            "applied": payload,
250	            "before": before.model_dump(mode="json"),
251	            "after": after.model_dump(mode="json"),
252	            "project": result,
253	        },
254	    }
255	
256	
257	async def assign_security_policy_to_projects(
258	    ctx: Context,
259	    security_policy_id: int,
260	    project_locators: list[str],
261	) -> dict[str, Any]:
262	    """
263	    Assign one FOSSA security policy to several projects at once.
264	
265	    WRITES TO FOSSA. Requires FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES=true.
266	
267	    Assignment only. Unlike fossa_enable_security_policy this does not touch
268	    scanning or the status check, because the bulk endpoint cannot set them —
269	    a project that has scanning switched off will take the policy and still
270	    block nothing.
271	
272	    This tool deliberately does not expose the endpoint's "apply to all projects
273	    matching these filters" mode. Every target must be named explicitly.
274	    """
275	    if security_policy_id < 1:
276	        raise ValueError("security_policy_id must be >= 1")
277	    if not project_locators:
278	        raise ValueError("project_locators must name at least one project")
279	    if any(not locator.strip() for locator in project_locators):
280	        raise ValueError("project_locators must not contain blank entries")
281	
282	    lifespan_ctx = ctx.request_context.lifespan_context
283	    client: FossaClient = lifespan_ctx["client"]
284	    settings: Settings = lifespan_ctx["settings"]
285	
286	    require_tier(settings, WriteTier.WRITE, "fossa_assign_security_policy_to_projects")
287	
288	    params: list[tuple[str, str]] = [("policyId", str(security_policy_id))]
289	    for locator in project_locators:
290	        params.append(("locators[]", locator))
291	
292	    result = await client.request_json("PUT", "/v2/projects/policy", params=params)
293	
294	    # The endpoint answers with a map of locator -> error for the ones that
295	    # failed, and an empty object when everything succeeded. Surface that
296	    # distinction rather than reporting a blanket success.
297	    failures = result if isinstance(result, dict) else {}
298	
299	    return {
300	        "ok": True,
301	        "endpoint": "PUT /v2/projects/policy",
302	        "data": {
303	            "security_policy_id": security_policy_id,
304	            "requested": project_locators,
305	            "failures": failures,
306	            "succeeded": [locator for locator in project_locators if locator not in failures],
307	        },
308	    }

25	# an edit. GET is read-only; PUT and DELETE assign or remove a named resource,
26	# so a replay converges on the same state.
27	_IDEMPOTENT_METHODS = frozenset({"GET", "HEAD", "PUT", "DELETE"})

30	class FossaClient:
31	    """Asynchronous FOSSA API client.
32	
33	    Owns a single reusable `httpx.AsyncClient` and connection pool for the
34	    lifetime of the server process.
35	    """
36	
37	    def __init__(self, settings: Settings, transport: httpx.AsyncBaseTransport | None = None):
38	        """
39	        Initialize the FOSSA client.
40	
41	        Args:
42	            settings: Application settings
43	            transport: Optional HTTP transport for testing
44	        """
45	        self.settings = settings
46	
47	        headers = {
48	            "User-Agent": f"fossa-mcp/{__version__}",
49	            "Accept": "application/json",
50	        }
51	        if settings.fossa_api_token:
52	            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {settings.fossa_api_token}"
53	
54	        self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
55	            base_url=settings.base_url,
56	            timeout=settings.fossa_timeout_seconds,
57	            verify=settings.fossa_verify_tls,
58	            transport=transport,
59	            headers=headers,
60	            limits=httpx.Limits(max_connections=20, max_keepalive_connections=10),
61	        )
62	
63	    async def request_json(
64	        self,
65	        method: str,
66	        path: str,
67	        *,
68	        params: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
69	        json_body: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
70	    ) -> dict[str, Any] | list[Any]:
71	        """
72	        Make an HTTP request and return the parsed JSON response.
73	
74	        Raises:
75	            FossaApiError: If the API returns an error or an invalid JSON body.
76	        """
77	        _, body = await self.request_json_with_status(
78	            method, path, params=params, json_body=json_body
79	        )
80	        return body
81	
82	    async def request_json_with_status(
83	        self,
84	        method: str,
85	        path: str,
86	        *,
87	        params: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
88	        json_body: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
89	    ) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any] | list[Any]]:
90	        """
91	        Make an HTTP request and return `(status_code, parsed_json)`.
92	
93	        Useful for endpoints where a specific 2xx status code (e.g. FOSSA's
94	        `202` "analysis in progress") is distinct from ordinary success and
95	        must not be discarded.
96	
97	        Raises:
98	            FossaApiError: If the API returns an error or an invalid JSON body.
99	        """
100	        response = await self._request(method, path, params=params, json_body=json_body)
101	
102	        if 200 <= response.status_code < 300:
103	            try:
104	                return response.status_code, response.json()
105	            except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
106	                raise FossaApiError(
107	                    status_code=response.status_code,
108	                    message="Invalid JSON response from FOSSA API",
109	                    method=method,
110	                    path=path,
111	                ) from exc
112	
113	        raise self._build_error(response, method, path)
114	
115	    async def request_text(
116	        self,
117	        method: str,
118	        path: str,
119	        *,
120	        params: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
121	    ) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
122	        """
123	        Make an HTTP request and return the raw text response.
124	
125	        Raises:
126	            FossaApiError: If the API returns an error.
127	        """
128	        response = await self._request(method, path, params=params)
129	
130	        if 200 <= response.status_code < 300:
131	            return response.text, response.headers.get("content-type")
132	
133	        raise self._build_error(response, method, path)
134	
135	    async def _request(
136	        self,
137	        method: str,
138	        path: str,
139	        *,
140	        params: list[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
141	        json_body: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
142	    ) -> httpx.Response:
143	        """Perform the HTTP call, retrying transient failures per the retry policy.
144	
145	        Retries are **method-aware**. `POST` and `PATCH` are never replayed after
146	        an in-flight failure: the request may well have been applied before the
147	        connection died, and replaying it would create a second team, a second
148	        service account, or apply an edit twice. Those methods surface the
149	        timeout to the caller instead, who can decide whether re-issuing is
150	        safe. See `_IDEMPOTENT_METHODS`.
151	
152	        A retryable *status code* (502/503/504) is different — the server
153	        answered and told us it did not process the request — so that path
154	        retries for every method.
155	        """
156	        # httpx's QueryParamTypes list branch is invariant on
157	        # list[tuple[str, str]]; its homogeneous-tuple branch is covariant, so
158	        # pass a plain tuple instead of relying on structural list compatibility.
159	        httpx_params = tuple(params) if params else None
160	        replayable = method.upper() in _IDEMPOTENT_METHODS
161	
162	        attempt = 0
163	        while True:
164	            try:
165	                response = await self._client.request(
166	                    method, path, params=httpx_params, json=json_body
167	                )
168	            except httpx.TimeoutException as exc:
169	                if replayable and attempt < _MAX_RETRIES:
170	                    await self._sleep_backoff(attempt)
171	                    attempt += 1
172	                    continue
173	                raise FossaApiError(
174	                    status_code=0,
175	                    message=(
176	                        f"FOSSA request timed out after {self.settings.fossa_timeout_seconds} "
177	                        f"seconds while calling {method} {path}."
178	                        + (
179	                            ""
180	                            if replayable
181	                            else " It was not retried because a replayed "
182	                            f"{method.upper()} could apply the change twice; it may or may not "
183	                            "have been applied."
184	                        )
185	                    ),
186	                    method=method,
187	                    path=path,
188	                ) from exc
189	            except httpx.TransportError as exc:
190	                if replayable and attempt < _MAX_RETRIES:
191	                    await self._sleep_backoff(attempt)
192	                    attempt += 1
193	                    continue
194	                raise FossaApiError(
195	                    status_code=0,
196	                    message=f"FOSSA request failed while calling {method} {path}: {exc}",
197	                    method=method,
198	                    path=path,
199	                ) from exc
200	
201	            logger.info(
202	                "FOSSA %s %s -> %d%s",
203	                method,
204	                path,
205	                response.status_code,
206	                self._elapsed_suffix(response),
207	            )
208	
209	            if response.status_code in _RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES and attempt < _MAX_RETRIES:
210	                await self._sleep_backoff(attempt, response)
211	                attempt += 1
212	                continue
213	
214	            return response
215	
216	    async def _sleep_backoff(self, attempt: int, response: httpx.Response | None = None) -> None:
217	        """Sleep for the backoff delay, honoring a safe, short `Retry-After` if present."""
218	        delay = _BACKOFF_SECONDS[attempt]
219	
220	        if response is not None:
221	            retry_after = response.headers.get("retry-after")
222	            if retry_after is not None:
223	                try:
224	                    seconds = float(retry_after)
225	                except ValueError:
226	                    seconds = None
227	                if seconds is not None and 0 <= seconds <= _MAX_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS:
228	                    delay = seconds
229	
230	        logger.info("FOSSA retrying (attempt %d) after %.2fs", attempt + 1, delay)
231	        await asyncio.sleep(delay)
232	
233	    @staticmethod
234	    def _elapsed_suffix(response: httpx.Response) -> str:
235	        """Format elapsed time for logging; absent under mock transports."""
236	        try:
237	            elapsed_ms = response.elapsed.total_seconds() * 1000
238	        except RuntimeError:
239	            return ""
240	        return f" in {elapsed_ms:.0f}ms"
241	
242	    @staticmethod
243	    def _build_error(response: httpx.Response, method: str, path: str) -> FossaApiError:
244	        """Build a FossaApiError from an error response, parsing FOSSA's JSON error shape."""
245	        try:
246	            error_data = response.json()
247	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
248	            return FossaApiError(
249	                status_code=response.status_code,
250	                message=response.text or "Unknown error",
251	                method=method,
252	                path=path,
253	            )
254	
255	        return FossaApiError(
256	            status_code=response.status_code,
257	            message=error_data.get("message", "Unknown error"),
258	            error_name=error_data.get("name"),
259	            fossa_code=error_data.get("code"),
260	            reference_uuid=error_data.get("uuid"),
261	            method=method,
262	            path=path,
263	        )
264	
265	    async def aclose(self) -> None:
266	        """Close the HTTP client."""
267	        await self._client.aclose()
268

97	def _forbid_unexpected_tool_arguments(server: FastMCP) -> None:
98	    """Make tools reject unknown arguments instead of silently dropping them.
99	
100	    FastMCP 1.28 generates each tool's argument model with Pydantic's default
101	    `extra="ignore"`, so a client that passes a misspelled or invented argument
102	    gets a successful call with that argument discarded — an easy way for a
103	    model to believe it applied a filter that never reached FOSSA. Tighten every
104	    generated model and republish its JSON schema so `additionalProperties:
105	    false` is advertised too.
106	
107	    This reaches into the tool manager because 1.28 exposes no public hook. Fold
108	    it into tool registration when moving to the 2.x SDK (see DECISIONS.md).
109	    """
110	    for tool in server._tool_manager._tools.values():
111	        arg_model = tool.fn_metadata.arg_model
112	        arg_model.model_config["extra"] = "forbid"
113	        arg_model.model_rebuild(force=True)
114	        tool.parameters = arg_model.model_json_schema(by_alias=True)
115	
116	
117	_forbid_unexpected_tool_arguments(mcp)
118	
119	_ALLOWED_TRANSPORTS = ("stdio", "streamable-http")
120	
121	
122	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
123	    """CLI entry point for the FOSSA MCP server."""
124	    args = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
125	    transport = "stdio"
126	
127	    idx = 0
128	    while idx < len(args):
129	        arg = args[idx]
130	        if arg == "--transport":
131	            if idx + 1 >= len(args):
132	                raise ValueError("Missing transport value after --transport")
133	            transport = args[idx + 1]
134	            if transport not in _ALLOWED_TRANSPORTS:
135	                raise ValueError(f"Unknown transport: {transport}")
136	            idx += 2
137	        elif arg == "--version":
138	            print(f"fossa-mcp version {__version__}")
139	            return
140	        else:
141	            raise ValueError(f"Unknown argument: {arg}")
142	
143	    logging.basicConfig(
144	        level=settings.log_level_int,
145	        format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(levelname)s %(message)s",
146	        stream=sys.stderr,
147	    )
148	
149	    logger.info("Starting FOSSA MCP server with transport: %s", transport)
150	
151	    # mcp.run() is synchronous: it drives its own anyio event loop.
152	    mcp.run(transport=transport)

52	   signature), construct the model first to validate, then call `require_tier`, then build the
53	   request. **Gate before request construction, always.**
54	3. Registration in `server.py` with annotations matching the tier.
55	4. respx contract test — method, path, exact query pairs, exact JSON body.

60	### First move
61	
62	Projects, per the order of work below. Ten writes and ten reads, and it exercises every tier:
63	`PUT /projects/{locator}` is `WRITE`, `DELETE /projects/{locator}` is `DESTRUCTIVE`, and
64	`DELETE /v2/projects` is `DESTRUCTIVE` with an unbounded filter — the case the tier split exists
65	for.
66	
67	Read the spec entry before writing each one. `PUT /projects/{locator}` alone accepts 50 body
68	fields; do not infer them:
69	
70	```bash
71	python3 -c "
72	import json; s=json.load(open('spec/fossa-openapi.json'))
73	op=s['paths']['/projects/{locator}']['put']
74	print(json.dumps(op['requestBody'], indent=2))"

77	### Two known traps
78	
79	* **`GET /projects/{locator}` documents an empty response schema.** The 200 body has no declared
80	  properties in the spec, so field names must come from live responses — `securityPolicyId`,
81	  `securityIssueScanningEnabled` and friends were confirmed against a real call, not the spec.
82	  Expect the same gap elsewhere; verify reads against a live org before trusting a shape.
83	* **Locators need `quote(locator, safe="")`.** They contain `+`, `/`, and `$`. Note that

3	import logging
4	
5	from pydantic import Field, field_validator
6	from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
7	
8	_VALID_LOG_LEVELS = {"DEBUG", "INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR", "CRITICAL"}
9	
10	
11	class Settings(BaseSettings):
12	    """Settings for the FOSSA MCP server."""
13	
14	    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8")
15	
16	    # API credentials and connection
17	    fossa_api_token: str | None = Field(default=None, description="FOSSA API token")
18	    fossa_base_url: str = Field(
19	        default="https://app.fossa.com/api", description="Base FOSSA API URL"
20	    )
21	    fossa_timeout_seconds: float = Field(
22	        default=20.0, gt=0, description="Timeout for FOSSA requests in seconds"
23	    )
24	    fossa_verify_tls: bool = Field(default=True, description="Verify TLS certificates")
25	
26	    # Page size limits
27	    fossa_max_page_size: int = Field(
28	        default=100, ge=1, le=1000, description="Maximum page size for API calls"
29	    )
30	    fossa_report_max_chars: int = Field(
31	        default=200000,
32	        ge=1000,
33	        le=1000000,
34	        description="Maximum characters in attribution reports",
35	    )
36	
37	    # Policy enforcement
38	    fossa_policy_file: str | None = Field(
39	        default=None,
40	        description="Path to the local security policy overlay file (JSON)",
41	    )
42	    fossa_org_id: int | None = Field(
43	        default=None,
44	        description="FOSSA organization ID, required by the organization settings endpoints",
45	    )
46	    # Write gating is tiered, not one flag. Each tier is a strict superset of the
47	    # risk below it, and each must be enabled independently — enabling writes
48	    # never implies destructive, and destructive never implies admin.
49	    fossa_allow_writes: bool = Field(
50	        default=False,
51	        description=(
52	            "Permit tools that create or update FOSSA state. Off by default: every "
53	            "write tool refuses before issuing a request unless this is enabled."
54	        ),
55	    )
56	    fossa_allow_destructive: bool = Field(
57	        default=False,
58	        description=(
59	            "Permit tools that delete FOSSA state or act on an unbounded set of "
60	            "targets. Requires fossa_allow_writes as well."
61	        ),
62	    )
63	    fossa_allow_admin: bool = Field(
64	        default=False,
65	        description=(
66	            "Permit tools that change identity, authentication, or access control "
67	            "(SAML, OIDC, roles, service accounts, team membership). Requires "
68	            "fossa_allow_writes as well."
69	        ),
70	    )
71	
72	    # Logging
73	    fossa_log_level: str = Field(default="INFO", description="Log level for the application")
74	
75	    # HTTP transport
76	    fossa_http_host: str = Field(
77	        default="127.0.0.1", description="HTTP host for streamable HTTP transport"
78	    )
79	    fossa_http_port: int = Field(
80	        default=8000, ge=1, le=65535, description="HTTP port for streamable HTTP transport"
81	    )
82	
83	    @field_validator("fossa_log_level")
84	    @classmethod
85	    def _validate_log_level(cls, value: str) -> str:
86	        """Ensure the configured log level is a valid Python log level name."""
87	        normalized = value.upper()
88	        if normalized not in _VALID_LOG_LEVELS:
89	            raise ValueError(
90	                f"fossa_log_level must be one of {sorted(_VALID_LOG_LEVELS)}, got {value!r}"
91	            )
92	        return normalized
93	
94	    @field_validator("fossa_base_url")
95	    @classmethod
96	    def _strip_trailing_slash(cls, value: str) -> str:
97	        return value.rstrip("/")
98	
99	    @field_validator("fossa_api_token")
100	    @classmethod
101	    def _strip_token_whitespace(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
102	        """Tolerate surrounding whitespace in the supplied token.
103	
104	        Tokens routinely arrive from a file or a Kubernetes Secret created with
105	        `--from-file`, both of which keep the trailing newline. Sending that
106	        newline in the Authorization header fails every request with a 401 that
107	        looks like a bad token rather than a bad newline. An empty or
108	        whitespace-only value is treated as absent.
109	        """
110	        if value is None:
111	            return None
112	        stripped = value.strip()
113	        return stripped or None
114	
115	    @field_validator("fossa_policy_file")
116	    @classmethod
117	    def _normalize_policy_file(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
118	        """Treat an empty or whitespace-only path as absent, like the token."""
119	        if value is None:
120	            return None
121	        stripped = value.strip()
122	        return stripped or None
123	
124	    @property
125	    def base_url(self) -> str:
126	        """Get the base URL without a trailing slash. Already includes `/api`."""
127	        return self.fossa_base_url
128	
129	    @property
130	    def log_level_int(self) -> int:
131	        """Resolve the configured log level name to its numeric value."""
132	        return logging.getLevelNamesMapping()[self.fossa_log_level]

1	# FOSSA MCP Server
2	[![FOSSA Status](https://app.fossa.com/api/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Fdarthzen%2Ffossa-mcp.svg?type=shield)](https://app.fossa.com/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Fdarthzen%2Ffossa-mcp?ref=badge_shield)
3	
4	
5	A Model Context Protocol server for the FOSSA API that allows AI assistants to inspect FOSSA organizations and answer practical software composition analysis questions.
6	
7	> **Unofficial project.** Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by FOSSA, Inc. "FOSSA" is a
8	> trademark of FOSSA, Inc., used here only to identify the API this software interoperates with. For
9	> the official product and support, see [fossa.com](https://fossa.com).
10	
11	## Safety Statement
12	
13	**Almost every tool is read-only. Two are not.**
14	
15	`fossa_enable_security_policy` and `fossa_assign_security_policy_to_projects` change which FOSSA
16	security policy governs a project and whether it blocks builds. Every other tool only reads.
17	
18	Writes are **off by default**. Both write tools refuse before issuing any request unless the
19	operator sets `FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES=true`. Leave it off on any instance that does not need to change
20	policy assignments — under the single-tenant model below, everyone who reaches this server shares
21	one token and therefore its write access too.
22	
23	See [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) §5 for why the earlier read-only guarantee was dropped.
24	
25	## Deployment model — single-tenant
26	
27	**This server is designed to be run by one operator with one FOSSA API token.** You run your own
28	instance; there is no multi-user mode.
29	
30	⚠️ **The server executes every request using the single `FOSSA_API_TOKEN` it was started with.** It
31	does not authenticate callers or scope requests per user. If you expose the HTTP transport to other
32	people, every one of them gets the full access of that token — including anything it can read across
33	your FOSSA organization.
34	
35	- `stdio` is the default transport and the intended deployment shape: your MCP client launches the
36	  process, and the token stays local to it.
37	- `streamable-http` binds `127.0.0.1` by default and is intended for local or sidecar use. Do not
38	  put it on a shared network interface without an authenticating proxy in front of it.
39	
40	## Requirements
41	
42	- Python 3.13+
43	- `uv`
44	- Full FOSSA API token for live calls
45	- Node/npm only when launching MCP Inspector through `mcp dev`
46	
47	## Setup
48	
49	```bash
50	git clone <repo>
51	cd fossa-mcp
52	uv sync
53	cp .env.example .env
54	```
55	
56	Then edit `.env` and add your FOSSA API token:
57	
58	```dotenv
59	FOSSA_API_TOKEN=<your-full-api-token>
60	```
61	
62	## Validate
63	
64	```bash
65	uv run pytest
66	uv run ruff check .
67	uv run ruff format --check .
68	uv run pyright
69	```
70	
71	`pytest` never touches the network; the live smoke test is opt-in via `uv run pytest -m live` and
72	needs a real `FOSSA_API_TOKEN`.
73	
74	## MCP Inspector
75	
76	```bash
77	uv run mcp dev src/fossa_mcp/server.py
78	```
79	
80	## stdio
81	
82	```bash
83	uv run fossa-mcp
84	```
85	
86	## Streamable HTTP
87	
88	```bash
89	uv run fossa-mcp --transport streamable-http
90	```
91	
92	## Container
93	
94	```bash
95	docker run --rm -i -e FOSSA_API_TOKEN=<your-full-api-token> rashford/fossa-mcp:0.1
96	```
97	
98	For `streamable-http`, publish the port and override the default `CMD`:
99	
100	```bash
101	docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 -e FOSSA_API_TOKEN=<your-full-api-token> \
102	  rashford/fossa-mcp:0.1 --transport streamable-http
103	```
104	
105	Images are tagged `:0.1.0` and `:0.1`. `:latest` is intentionally not published until a release has
106	soaked — see [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md).
107	
108	Every image ships `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, and a consolidated `/app/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt` covering
109	every runtime dependency actually installed in that image, generated at build time by
110	`scripts/generate_third_party_licenses.py`.
111	
112	## Tools
113	
114	| Tool | Description |
115	|------|-------------|
116	| `fossa_list_projects` | List FOSSA projects visible to the current account |
117	| `fossa_get_project` | Get detailed metadata about exactly one FOSSA project |
118	| `fossa_list_project_revisions` | List analyzed revisions, branches, or tags for a project |
119	| `fossa_list_dependencies` | List dependencies detected in a specific project revision |
120	| `fossa_get_dependency` | Get the richer detail record for one dependency in one revision |
121	| `fossa_list_issues` | Query licensing, vulnerability, or quality issues globally or for one project revision |
122	| `fossa_get_issue` | Retrieve complete detail for one issue |
123	| `fossa_project_posture` | Provide one high-value, model-friendly view of a project revision's current FOSSA issue posture |
124	| `fossa_get_attribution_report` | Retrieve a text-friendly FOSSA attribution/SBOM report for a revision |
125	| `fossa_get_security_policy` | Show the security policy in force for a project: FOSSA's baseline plus the local overlay |
126	| `fossa_evaluate_security_policy` | Return an allow/warn/block verdict per dependency for a revision |
127	| `fossa_enable_security_policy` | **Writes.** Assign a security policy to a project and enable the enforcement that blocks violating packages |
128	| `fossa_assign_security_policy_to_projects` | **Writes.** Assign one security policy to several named projects |
129	
130	## Security policies
131	
132	FOSSA blocks a package through a combination of three settings: an assigned **security policy**
133	(what counts as a violation), **security issue scanning** (finding violations), and the **security
134	status check** (failing the build). `fossa_enable_security_policy` sets all three — that combination
135	is the block. FOSSA exposes no per-package block primitive.
136	
137	Policies are authored in the FOSSA web app. The API has no create-policy or list-policies endpoint,
138	so a policy is addressed by the numeric id in its FOSSA URL.
139	
140	### Local overlay
141	
142	`FOSSA_POLICY_FILE` points at a JSON file of local rules layered on top of FOSSA's own findings.
143	The overlay is **tighten-only**: it can block packages FOSSA currently allows, and it can never
144	clear a package FOSSA has raised an active vulnerability against.
145	
146	```json
147	{
148	  "version": 1,
149	  "security": [
150	    {
151	      "id": "no-high-severity",
152	      "description": "Stricter than the org-wide FOSSA policy",
153	      "enabled": true,
154	      "rules": {
155	        "max_cvss": 7.0,
156	        "warn_cvss": 4.0,
157	        "deny_severity": ["critical"],
158	        "denied_cves": ["CVE-2025-53365"],
159	        "denied_packages": ["left-pad", "npm+event-stream"]
160	      },
161	      "exceptions": [
162	        {
163	          "package": "pip+requests$2.31",
164	          "reason": "Vendored fork, patch applied out of band",
165	          "expires": "2026-12-31"
166	        }
167	      ]
168	    }
169	  ]
170	}
171	```
172	
173	`denied_packages` and `exceptions[].package` accept a full locator (`pip+mcp$1.6.0`, that version
174	only), a fetcher-qualified name (`pip+mcp`, any version), or a bare name (`mcp`, any fetcher).
175	
176	An exception requires a `reason` and suppresses only overlay-introduced blocks. Once `expires`
177	passes it stops applying and is reported on the verdict, so a package never silently reverts to
178	blocked without explanation. A configured-but-unreadable policy file is an error, not a fallback to
179	"no policy".
180	
181	### Turning enforcement on
182	
183	```bash
184	FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES=true uv run fossa-mcp
185	```
186	
187	Check what a policy would do before enabling it — `fossa_evaluate_security_policy` is read-only and
188	answers exactly that.
189	
190	## Example Prompts
191	
192	```text

"""Package block/unblock tools for the FOSSA MCP server.

These two tools sit on endpoints FOSSA does not document. They were captured
from the FOSSA web app's own traffic and verified against the live API; the
reasoning, the request schemas, and what was tried and rejected are recorded in
`docs/ENDPOINT_INFERENCE.md`. FOSSA owes no stability on them: the contract
tests in this repo pin *our* request shape and cannot detect FOSSA changing its
side, so both tools fail loudly rather than degrade quietly when a response
stops matching.

What the API actually does, and why the two tools are not mirror images:

* **Block is package-scoped and additive.** `POST /packages/{locator}/rules`
  attaches a `blacklisted_dependency` rule to each named policy. Re-posting an
  identical block reuses the same rule id rather than duplicating it, so the
  operation is idempotent.
* **Unblock is policy-scoped and replaces the policy's entire rule set.**
  There is no delete for a single rule — `DELETE /packages/{locator}/rules` is
  a 404. `PUT /policies/{policyId}/rules` takes a bare top-level array of the
  rules that should survive, which is the policy editor's Save. Removing one
  block therefore means read-modify-write over every rule the policy has.

That last point is the design constraint of this module. FOSSA offers no ETag,
`If-Match`, or version precondition — `rulesHash` is returned but not accepted —
so two callers unblocking different packages at the same time silently clobber
each other, and the last writer reinstates whatever the other removed. Unblock
consequently reads the policy immediately before writing, reports the rule set
it is about to send, and is gated at the `DESTRUCTIVE` tier rather than `WRITE`.

Blocking lives on **quality** policies, not security policies. See the appendix
of `docs/ENDPOINT_INFERENCE.md`: DECISIONS.md §5's claim that FOSSA has no
per-package block primitive is wrong, and the security policy tools in
`policies.py` are not the blocking mechanism.
"""

from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import quote

from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context

from ..client import FossaClient
from ..config import Settings
from ..errors import FossaApiError
from ..models import PackageBlockInput, PackageUnblockInput
from ..writes import WriteTier, require_tier

# The rule type FOSSA creates for a blocked package. Every other rule type on a
# quality policy (outdated_dependency, risk_abandonware, …) is unrelated and
# must survive an unblock untouched.
BLOCK_RULE_TYPE = "blacklisted_dependency"


def _rule_summary(rule: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Condense one FOSSA rule to the fields that identify it.

    Rule objects are wide and a licensing policy can carry over a thousand of
    them, so the full objects are sent to FOSSA but only this summary is
    returned to the caller.
    """
    return {
        "rule_id": rule.get("ruleId"),
        "type": rule.get("type"),
        "package_locator": rule.get("packageProjectLocator"),
        "version_type": rule.get("dependencyFilterVersionType"),
        "enabled": rule.get("enabled"),
    }


def _policy_rules(policy: Any, path: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Extract the rule array from a policy body, or fail loudly.

    A silent `[]` here would send an empty rule set to `PUT /rules` and wipe
    every rule the policy has, so an unrecognized shape must raise instead.
    """
    if not isinstance(policy, dict) or not isinstance(policy.get("rules"), list):
        raise FossaApiError(
            status_code=200,
            message=(
                "FOSSA returned a policy without a 'rules' array. This endpoint is undocumented "
                "and may have changed; refusing to rewrite the policy's rules from a response "
                "that is not understood."
            ),
            method="GET",
            path=path,
            error_name="UnexpectedResponse",
        )

    rules = policy["rules"]
    if any(not isinstance(rule, dict) for rule in rules):
        raise FossaApiError(
            status_code=200,
            message="FOSSA returned a policy whose 'rules' array contains a non-object entry.",
            method="GET",
            path=path,
            error_name="UnexpectedResponse",
        )
    return rules


async def block_package(
    ctx: Context,
    package_locator: str,
    policy_ids: list[int],
    versions: list[str] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Block a package by adding a blocked-dependency rule to one or more FOSSA
    quality policies.

    WRITES TO FOSSA. Requires FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES=true.

    `package_locator` is the versionless locator, e.g. `pip+aiofile` or
    `npm+left-pad`. Omit `versions` to block every version; pass
    `versions=["3.11.1"]` to block only those. `policy_ids` are the numeric ids
    of QUALITY policies — a block rule cannot attach to a licensing, security,
    or SBOM policy. Use fossa_unblock_package to reverse it.

    Idempotent: re-blocking the same package on the same policy reuses the
    existing rule instead of adding a second one.

    This uses an endpoint FOSSA does not document, captured from its web app.
    It may change without notice.
    """
    validated = PackageBlockInput(
        package_locator=package_locator,
        policy_ids=policy_ids,
        versions=versions,
    )

    lifespan_ctx = ctx.request_context.lifespan_context
    client: FossaClient = lifespan_ctx["client"]
    settings: Settings = lifespan_ctx["settings"]

    require_tier(settings, WriteTier.WRITE, "fossa_block_package")

    # "ALL" is FOSSA's own spelling for every version. An empty array is also
    # accepted by the API and means the same thing, but the input model rejects
    # it so that "every version" is always an explicit choice.
    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
        "policyIds": validated.policy_ids,
        "versions": validated.versions if validated.versions is not None else "ALL",
    }

    encoded_locator = quote(validated.package_locator, safe="")
    result = await client.request_json(
        "POST", f"/packages/{encoded_locator}/rules", json_body=payload
    )

    return {
        "ok": True,
        "endpoint": "POST /packages/{locator}/rules",
        "data": {
            "package_locator": validated.package_locator,
            "policy_ids": validated.policy_ids,
            "versions": payload["versions"],
            "request_body": payload,
            "policy_versions": result,
        },
    }


async def unblock_package(
    ctx: Context,
    package_locator: str,
    policy_id: int,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Remove a package's blocked-dependency rule from one FOSSA quality policy.

    WRITES TO FOSSA, DESTRUCTIVELY. Requires FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES=true and
    FOSSA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true.

    FOSSA has no delete for a single rule. Unblocking rewrites the policy's
    entire rule set with the rules that should survive, and the API offers no
    precondition to make that safe — a second caller editing the same policy
    concurrently will silently undo this change, or have theirs undone. The
    surviving rules this tool is about to send are reported in
    `data.rules_sent`.

    Every rule that is not a block on `package_locator` is preserved. If the
    policy carries no such block, nothing is sent and the policy is left alone.

    This uses an endpoint FOSSA does not document, captured from its web app.
    It may change without notice.
    """
    validated = PackageUnblockInput(package_locator=package_locator, policy_id=policy_id)

    lifespan_ctx = ctx.request_context.lifespan_context
    client: FossaClient = lifespan_ctx["client"]
    settings: Settings = lifespan_ctx["settings"]

    require_tier(settings, WriteTier.DESTRUCTIVE, "fossa_unblock_package")

    # Read immediately before the write. The window between this GET and the PUT
    # is the whole of the concurrency risk, so nothing goes between them.
    policy_path = f"/policies/{validated.policy_id}"
    policy = await client.request_json("GET", policy_path)
    rules = _policy_rules(policy, policy_path)

    removed = [
        rule
        for rule in rules
        if rule.get("type") == BLOCK_RULE_TYPE
        and rule.get("packageProjectLocator") == validated.package_locator
    ]

    if not removed:
        blocked = sorted(
            str(rule.get("packageProjectLocator"))
            for rule in rules
            if rule.get("type") == BLOCK_RULE_TYPE
        )
        return {
            "ok": True,
            "endpoint": "GET /policies/{policyId}",
            "message": (
                f"Policy {validated.policy_id} has no block rule for "
                f"{validated.package_locator}; nothing was changed."
            ),
            "data": {
                "package_locator": validated.package_locator,
                "policy_id": validated.policy_id,
                "removed": [],
                "packages_blocked_by_this_policy": blocked,
            },
        }

    survivors = [rule for rule in rules if rule not in removed]

    result = await client.request_json(
        "PUT", f"{policy_path}/rules", json_body=[dict(rule) for rule in survivors]
    )

    return {
        "ok": True,
        "endpoint": "PUT /policies/{policyId}/rules",
        "data": {
            "package_locator": validated.package_locator,
            "policy_id": validated.policy_id,
            "removed": [_rule_summary(rule) for rule in removed],
            "rules_sent_count": len(survivors),
            "rules_sent": [_rule_summary(rule) for rule in survivors],
            "policy_versions": result,
        },
    }

These endpoints are undocumented (see `docs/ENDPOINT_INFERENCE.md`), so the
request shapes asserted here are the ones captured from FOSSA's own web app and
verified against the live API. Two of them are load-bearing and easy to get
wrong: the block body carries `versions` as the string `"ALL"` rather than an
array, and the unblock body is a **bare top-level array** — every wrapper object
tried against the live API returned an opaque 500.

What these tests cannot do is notice FOSSA changing its side. They pin our
request, not their contract.
"""

import json

import httpx
import pytest

from fossa_mcp.client import FossaClient
from fossa_mcp.config import Settings
from fossa_mcp.errors import FossaApiError, FossaWriteNotPermittedError
from fossa_mcp.tools import packages

PACKAGE = "pip+aiofile"
ENCODED_PACKAGE = "pip%2Baiofile"
POLICY_ID = 266648

BLOCK_URL = f"https://app.fossa.com/api/packages/{ENCODED_PACKAGE}/rules"
POLICY_URL = f"https://app.fossa.com/api/policies/{POLICY_ID}"
POLICY_RULES_URL = f"{POLICY_URL}/rules"

# Abridged from a real `GET /api/policies/266648`, keeping the fields the tools
# read and enough of the rest to prove rules are echoed back untouched.

    "ruleId": 58586851,
    "type": "blacklisted_dependency",
    "packageProjectLocator": PACKAGE,
    "dependencyFilterVersionType": "ALL",
    "dependencyFilterName": None,
    "dependencyFilterStartVersion": None,
    "dependencyFilterEndVersion": None,
    "enabled": True,
    "notes": None,
    "createdAt": "2026-07-31T20:01:41.871Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-07-31T20:01:41.871Z",

## Safety Statement

**Almost every tool is read-only. Four are not.**

`fossa_enable_security_policy` and `fossa_assign_security_policy_to_projects` change which FOSSA
security policy governs a project and whether it blocks builds. `fossa_block_package` and
`fossa_unblock_package` add and remove blocked-dependency rules on a quality policy. Every other

state — under the single-tenant model below, everyone who reaches this server shares one token and

## Security policies

FOSSA blocks a package through a combination of three settings: an assigned **security policy**
(what counts as a violation), **security issue scanning** (finding violations), and the **security
status check** (failing the build). `fossa_enable_security_policy` sets all three — that combination
is the block. FOSSA exposes no per-package block primitive.

Policies are authored in the FOSSA web app. The API has no create-policy or list-policies endpoint,
so a policy is addressed by the numeric id in its FOSSA URL.
input.new_string:
## Write operations

Write access is off by default and tiered. Each tier is enabled independently, and the higher ones
do not imply the lower: `FOSSA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true` on its own grants nothing, so a
half-configured deployment stays safe rather than becoming partly writable.

| Env var | Permits |
|---------|---------|
| `FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES` | Create and update. Required by every write tool. |
| `FOSSA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE` | Deletes, and operations whose target set is unbounded. Requires `FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES` as well. |

| Tool | Tier | Endpoint |
|------|------|----------|
| `fossa_enable_security_policy` | write | `PUT /projects/{locator}` |
| `fossa_assign_security_policy_to_projects` | write | `PUT /v2/projects/policy` |
| `fossa_block_package` | write | `POST /packages/{locator}/rules` |
| `fossa_unblock_package` | write + destructive | `GET /policies/{id}` then `PUT /policies/{id}/rules` |

The gate is checked inside the tool body before any request is constructed, so a refused call sends
nothing to FOSSA.

```bash
FOSSA_ALLOW_WRITES=true FOSSA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=true uv run fossa-mcp
```

### Blocking a package

```text
Block pip+aiofile on quality policy 266648.
```

`fossa_block_package` takes a **versionless** locator (`pip+aiofile`, not `pip+aiofile$1.2.3`) and
one or more QUALITY policy ids — a block rule cannot attach to a licensing, security, or SBOM
policy. Omit `versions` to block every version, or pass `versions=["3.11.1"]` to block only those.
Re-blocking is idempotent: FOSSA reuses the existing rule rather than adding a second one.

`fossa_unblock_package` reverses it, and is gated at the destructive tier for a reason. FOSSA has no
delete for a single rule — the only way to remove one is `PUT /policies/{id}/rules`, which replaces
the policy's **entire** rule set, and the API offers no ETag, `If-Match`, or version precondition to
make that safe. Two callers unblocking different packages at the same time silently clobber each
other. The tool reads the policy immediately before writing and reports the surviving rule set it
sent in `data.rules_sent`. If the policy has no matching block rule it changes nothing rather than
rewriting the rule set for no reason.

> ⚠️ **Both tools use endpoints FOSSA does not document**, captured from its web app's own traffic
> and verified against the live API. FOSSA owes no stability on them: they can change without notice
> or a version bump. The contract tests in this repo pin *our* request shape and cannot detect FOSSA
> changing its side, so both tools fail loudly rather than degrade quietly if a response stops
> matching. [docs/ENDPOINT_INFERENCE.md](docs/ENDPOINT_INFERENCE.md) records the request schemas,
> how they were derived, and what was tried and rejected.

## Security policies

An assigned **security policy** (what counts as a violation), **security issue scanning** (finding
violations), and the **security status check** (failing the build) are what make a vulnerability
fail a build. `fossa_enable_security_policy` sets all three.

That is distinct from blocking a specific package, which is a `blacklisted_dependency` rule on a
**quality** policy — see [Blocking a package](#blocking-a-package). The security policy tools do not
block packages by name.

Policies are authored in the FOSSA web app and addressed here by the numeric id in their FOSSA URL.
The vendored OpenAPI spec has no create-policy or list-policies operation, though the live API does
serve `GET /api/policies`; no tool wraps it yet.

additive, and idempotent — re-posting reuses the same rule id — so it is a WRITE
with idempotentHint=True. Unblock is policy-scoped: FOSSA has no delete for one
